meaning.implemented: Whole named entry point has Rust replacement, not just a prerequisite library.
meaning.reviewed: Independent source review of that replacement is recorded.
meaning.package_selected: Repository packaging selects the Rust replacement. This does not prove any live installation updated.
meaning.end_to_end_accepted: Supported installation and relevant full owner/agent workflow accepted on exact release artifacts. Protocol/library tests alone do not fill this column.

scope: All16 declared Python console entry points.
Selected installed/generated broker, runtime/model, optional OPS/cleanup variants and extensionless autoenv entries audited directly in pinned Nix source.
Already merged Rust entry points, retaining a distinction between package selection and installed acceptance.
All eight top-level broker request kinds J/L/C/G/T/M/Y/Q are recorded separately from the native client implementation.
limits: Starting runtime supplement to the application surface inventory, not an exhaustive transitive Python/runtime/build/owner-tool audit.

Duplicate external commands in distinct package variants retain one coverage_unit for deduplication. Protocol and command rows are different units; do not calculate a whole-port percentage by summing heterogeneous rows.
Declared console entries and optional packages need active/opt-in/retired caller disposition before obsolete code is ported or retired.
UNASSIGNED is an ownership gap, not a grant or a new assignment.
Mutable WIP is not marked implemented; readiness must bind exact reviewed artifacts.
Source lines belong to sourceRevision and must be revalidated when that revision changes.
